message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Kentucky Avenue.

I'm in jail with $1,179. The current high bid is $41 by p4. I have no monopolies. p1 dropped out after holding only $15 cash.

p3 has Illinois and p4 has Indiana. Kentucky would complete no set for anyone currently. I have no reds.

I should bid around $60 to block p3 from holding two reds. p4 can only raise to $74, and p3 has $97 or mortgaged railroads. I'll drop above roughly $110 to let them drain cash. Boardwalk is only two houses, so I need about $970 for jail exit and a green house level.

p3 would still need Indiana from p1 to complete the red set. p4 has no set synergy with Kentucky and is bidding aggressively for a property that does not help them. The mortgage value is $110, so winning at $42 to $70 is reasonable.

Dropping and letting p3 win would drain their cash. They currently hold a strong pink monopoly and four railroads. That is valuable.

I am in jail for two of three turns. I recently collected $22 rent from p3 on their pink properties. They may want to even out those houses.

The auction was started by p1 after landing on Kentucky. I am still in jail with two turns remaining. I need to check whether the next roll must be doubles or if I will pay $50 and leave.

I rolled at turn 89 without doubles. With two jail turns already spent, the next roll may be my third and final chance to escape, or I may be forced to pay $50.

The $50 jail fee is negligible against my $1,179 cash. p4's Boardwalk with two houses yields $600 in rent. p3's pink properties with three houses each generate $180, $550, and $600 in rent, plus $200 from the four railroads.

p1's orange properties generate $150, $550, and $220 in rent. They sold a house to pay railroad rent and now have only $15 cash, so they likely cannot rebuild.

Pennsylvania Avenue is unowned at $320. I own Pacific and North Carolina, so completing the green set would give me a strong monopoly. Even with one house on each green, rent is $130, $130, and $150. Building evenly to three houses would cost $1,800, which I do not have yet.

I should cap my bid at the $110 mortgage value. I need to keep roughly $970 in cash for jail exit and a potential $320 purchase of Pennsylvania Avenue. Even a $42 bid leaves me with $1,137, and a $110 bid leaves $1,069. I am now questioning whether blocking p3 from two reds is worth paying above the mortgage value.

Blocking p3 from two reds is worth something, but not $150. I should stay in the auction and raise the price to drain p4 and p3, then drop near my cap so the winner overpays. If p4 wins at a high price, they only have $74.

Draining p4 would prevent them from building more houses on Boardwalk and Park Place, since they currently hold two houses on Boardwalk and one on Park Place. If p3 wins at a high price, their $97 cash would be spent and they could not rebuild their pink properties. Winning cheap would give me the property but would not drain my opponents.

I will bid $42, the minimum raise, to stay in the auction. I should continue the "no set" narrative to discourage p3 and p4 from raising further. A minimum bid is more efficient than a larger raise because it keeps control without overpaying if both opponents drop.

I am the one inflating the bid. If I drop now, p3 may outbid p4 and win around $75 for a non-monopoly property. That would leave p3 with only $22 cash.

p3 cannot build another house on their pink properties because each costs $100 and they only have $97. Their railroads are not mortgaged, so draining their cash would mainly hurt rent survival rather than construction. My own properties would not pose a lethal threat to them.

p4 cannot build to three houses on Boardwalk or Park Place because each house costs $200 and they only have $74. I can afford the $600 rent from Boardwalk, so p4 would still be vulnerable even if they win the auction.
